messages:
Maya (devex): heads up — hitting SSL cert verify errors when pip installing our python sdk inside a Windows venv (py3.11 and py3.8 repro'd). error: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed`
Sam (sdk): ugh, can you paste the exact pip command + traceback? are you behind corp proxy?
Maya (devex): repro steps:
1) `python -m venv .venv && .\\.venv\\Scripts\\activate`
2) `pip install --upgrade pip`
3) `pip install redwood-inference`
Traceback snippet: `urllib3.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:1123)`
Liam (windows): do you see `CERT_INVALID` or a cert path? windows has multiple cert stores — sometimes pip uses a bundled OpenSSL which ignores Windows certs. what does `python -c "import ssl, certifi; print(ssl.get_default_verify_paths())"` show?
Maya (devex): output looks like:
`DefaultVerifyPaths(cafile=None, capath=None, openssl_cafile_env=None, openssl_cafile=None, openssl_capath_env=None, openssl_capath=None)`
Jess (qa): repro on 3.8/3.12 too? we saw similar in CI last month but on linux only.
Maya (devex): yes 3.8/3.11/3.12 on Windows 10/11. CI (linux) is fine.
Sam (sdk): likely two issues colliding: (A) our wheel on Windows isn't providing a compatible OpenSSL or metadata so pip falls back to source and the build environment lacks certs, (B) our package doesn't expose a `ca_bundle` fallback env var. quick workaround: `pip install certifi && set SSL_CERT_FILE=%(CERTIFI)s` where `%(CERTIFI)s` is path from `python -c "import certifi;print(certifi.where())"`. that should unblock.
Liam (windows): also try `python -m pip install --upgrade setuptools wheel` — sometimes building from sdist fails and pip uses system OpenSSL which is weird on windows.
Maya (devex): workaround worked after `pip install certifi` — thanks. but we need a proper fix for onboarding docs and wheels. users on windows won't know this.
Sam (sdk): agreed. action items: 1) produce official wheels for cp38-cp312-win_amd64 so pip won't build from sdist, 2) ship a small cert bundle fallback and honor `REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE` env var or `ssl` override, 3) add note in quickstart for Windows venv certifi step.
Jess (qa): and add a regression test matrix for py3.8-3.12 windows + azure pipelines. we can add a smoke install job.
Maya (devex): another small DX bug — typing stubs: `AsyncClient` has no typed overloads so mypy users get `Any` and autocomplete is weak. can we publish PEP 561-compatible stubs?
Sam (sdk): yes, we should. we have a separate request for stubs. prioritize together with wheels + certs. I'll file one GH meta-issue and link the PRs.
pip-bot: published issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/412 (windows wheels + cert bundle + typing stubs) :rocket:
Liam (windows): quick note for the issue: include which MSVC toolchain used to build wheels, and ensure we build with OpenSSLx.y that matches manylinux equivalent to reduce runtime diffs.
Sam (sdk): assigning to @sam to coordinate builds, @liam for Windows infra, @jess for QA matrix. thanks all — putting this on the sprint. :shipit:
Maya (devex): adding a quick doc snippet for the Windows quickstart now and will PR to docs repo. :eyes:
